exposure: Presence or absence of symptomatic pelvic floor disorders
outcome: maternal recall of mode of delivery
maternal recall of prolonged second stage of labor
maternal recall of spontaneous perineal laceration
maternal recall of anal sphincter laceration
cohort: 1011 women from the Mothers' Outcomes After Delivery study, including 1821 deliveries
finding: While maternal recall was generally accurate for most obstetric events, women with symptomatic pelvic floor disorders were more likely to report a history of anal sphincter laceration, regardless of medical record documentation.
